subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept this one-way PortGuardian storage cutover, including fail-closed coexistence with older JSON-writing macOS copies and no supported downgrade path after SQLite receipts are created?
rationale: The implementation intentionally changes the operational upgrade contract for machine-global tunnel recovery; tests can validate mechanics but cannot choose whether the compatibility tradeoff is acceptable.

options.title: Accept the bounded one-way cutover
options.body: Approve the SQLite-only runtime after the prerequisite lands and final-head signed migration proof is attached, accepting that older JSON-only copies must not share the migrated state directory.

options.title: Require a different upgrade policy
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers define a supported downgrade or coexistence strategy, then revise the migration boundary and proof accordingly.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded one-way cutover
recommendation.body: Approve the SQLite-only runtime after the prerequisite lands and final-head signed migration proof is attached, accepting that older JSON-only copies must not share the migrated state directory.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor authored the stack and documented the exact compatibility contract requiring maintainer sponsorship; confidence is limited because local ownership history could not be inspected.
